test_title: PYST 34 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 25 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

She said that by the next month, she would have been living in Paris for five years.

options.text: She said, "By next month, I will have been living in Paris for five years.
She said, "By next month, I would be living in Paris for five years."
She said, "By next month, I have been living in Paris for five years."
She said, "By the next month, I will live in Paris for five years."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that by the next month, she would have been living in Paris for five years.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"would have been living" becomes "will have been living"**
 
 
• In direct speech, the future perfect continuous tense is used to indicate an ongoing action that will be completed by a certain point in the future.
 
• The modal verb "would" is replaced by "will" to reflect direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"she" becomes "I"**
 
 
• Pronoun change is necessary to match the perspective of the speaker in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"by the next month" remains "by next month"**
 
 
• The time expression is simplified for natural usage in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "By" and ends with a period "." inside the quotation marks.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"By next month, I will have been living in Paris for five years."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "By next month, I would be living in Paris for five years."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "would be living" is not the correct future perfect continuous form.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "By next month, I have been living in Paris for five years."
 
 
• Tense mismatch: "have been living" is present perfect continuous, not future perfect continuous.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "By the next month, I will live in Paris for five years."
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "will live" does not convey the ongoing action as required in future perfect continuous.
